record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every finite orientably regular d-polytope, for d ≥ 2, admit a finite chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 28 Does every orientably regular finite d-polytope admit a finite chiral extension (d ≥ 2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $d$ is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) are graded by rank from $-1$ to $d$, satisfying the standard axioms: it has a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face; every maximal chain (flag) has exactly $d+2$ elements; it is strongly flag-connected; and it satisfies the diamond condition (for any two faces $F<G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$). The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts freely on flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is regular if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on flags. It is chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits. A regular polytope is orientably regular if its automorphism group has a subgroup of index 2 that acts transitively on flags of one of the two classes obtained by the natural 2-coloring of adjacent flags (equivalently, the rotation subgroup has index 2). A chiral (or regular) $(d+1)$-polytope $\mathcal{Q}$ is called a chiral extension of a $d$-polytope $\mathcal{K}$ if $\mathcal{Q}$ is chiral and all its facets (rank-$d$ faces, viewed as $d$-polytopes) are isomorphic to $\mathcal{K}$.

Question: For every integer $d\ge 2$ and every finite orientably regular $d$-polytope $\mathcal{K}$, does there exist a finite chiral $(d+1)$-polytope $\mathcal{Q}$ whose facets are all isomorphic to $\mathcal{K}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists: Cunningham and Pellicer showed that every finite chiral $d$-polytope with regular facets has a finite chiral extension, and Montero and others have refined constructions controlling the Schläfli symbol. However, the general question of whether every finite orientably regular $d$-polytope (for $d\ge 2$) admits a finite chiral extension does not appear to be resolved in the literature, and it continues to be listed among open problems on chiral polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer)
status_evidence.snippet: Given a chiral d-polytope K with regular facets, a construction for a chiral (d+1)-polytope P with facets K is given; P is finite if K is.
status_evidence.claim: Finite chiral extensions exist for finite chiral polytopes with regular facets, but the question for orientably regular base polytopes is a separate listed problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes (Montero)
status_evidence.snippet: New constructions for chiral extensions with control on the Schläfli symbol, building on the Cunningham–Pellicer construction.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses control of Schläfli symbol but does not settle the orientably-regular base case in full generality.
